title: Overfitting

plan.insight: More flexible models keep lowering training error, but test error turns back up once they fit the noise.
plan.user_changes: polynomial degree, noise level, drag training points
plan.reacts: fitted curve, train/test error vs degree, current errors

init:
const gen = (n) => range(n).map(() => { const x = rand() * 2 - 1; return [x, Math.sin(Math.PI * x) + randn(0, state.noise)]; });
return { train: gen(14), test: gen(40) };

components.label: Noise
components.onChange:
const gen = (n) => range(n).map(() => { const x = rand() * 2 - 1; return [x, Math.sin(Math.PI * x) + randn(0, value)]; });
return { noise: value, train: gen(14), test: gen(40) };

components.title: Fit (drag training points)
components.onDrag: return { train: state.train.map((p, i) => i === index ? [pos.x, pos.y] : p) };

components.title: Error vs degree

components.label: Train MSE
components.value:
const c = polyfit(state.train.map((p) => p[0]), state.train.map((p) => p[1]), state.deg);
return mse(state.train.map((p) => polyval(c, p[0])), state.train.map((p) => p[1]));

components.label: Test MSE
components.value:
const c = polyfit(state.train.map((p) => p[0]), state.train.map((p) => p[1]), state.deg);
return mse(state.test.map((p) => polyval(c, p[0])), state.test.map((p) => p[1]));
